name: Secure Element and NFC platform access
plain: Reads and writes applets in the phone's secure chip for keys, badges and payments.
meaning: The secure element holds the strongest credentials on the phone. Third-party access means banks, car makers and employers can issue keys without Apple or Google Wallet.

android.permission: Open Mobile API: SE_PERMISSION via access rules (ARA); android.hardware.se.omapi
android.prompt_ui: Access rules on the SE grant per app signature
android.note: Third-party use needs the SE vendor's access rules; OEM wallets and carriers use it. Most apps use HCE instead.

ios.prompt_ui: Apple entitlement plus commercial agreement; fee applies
ios.note: Offered in selected countries (Australia, Brazil, Canada, Japan, NZ, UK, US at launch) and EEA under DMA terms.

limits.headline: Can use the phone's secure chip only with special approval
limits.user_action: You add a car key, work badge or bank credential from the issuer's app
can: Store keys, badges and payment credentials on the secure chip
Let banks, car makers and employers issue keys without Apple or Google Wallet
Run on iPhone in selected countries and the EEA
cannot: Use the chip on iPhone without Apple's entitlement, agreement and fee
Use the chip on Android without the chip vendor's access rules
Be used by most Android apps, which use host card emulation instead
limits.differs: iPhone needs an Apple entitlement and fee in selected countries; Android needs access rules from the chip vendor, so wallets and carriers mostly use it.

story.what_it_is: Lets an approved app store and run keys, badges and payment cards inside the phone's tamper proof chip.

marketing.name: NFC and SE Platform
marketing.pitch: Approved apps can use the phone's secure element for tap payments, car keys, IDs and more.

story.for_you: You tap your phone on a hotel door, a car or a payment reader and it works as fast as a card. The key is held in a locked chip, so someone who copies your app cannot copy the key.
story.for_makers: The chip is the safest place on a phone for car keys, bank cards and access badges. Banks, car makers and employers want to use it for their own brand. Platforms limit it to vetted companies and regions.

use_cases.example: A car maker's app opens and starts the car from the phone's secure chip.
A hotel app issues a room key valid for exactly your stay.
An employer's app holds a badge for the office door and the parking gate.
A student ID opens dorms and pays at the cafeteria.
A bank puts its own card in its app and takes taps without the system wallet.
A government app holds a digital ID checked by tapping a reader.
A home lock holds a house key and shares it with family.

story.android_note: Most Android apps use software card emulation. Third party secure chip access needs rules set by the chip owner.
story.ios_note: Apple offers it in selected countries (including Australia, Brazil, Canada, Japan, New Zealand, the UK and the US) and in the EEA under European law.

technical_bounds: Both vendors gate this by contract, not by a user prompt

history.change: Open Mobile API available to apps with SE access rules
SE credentials and NFC controller access for approved developers
